newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Stals says in fx control talks with govt.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Stals says in fx control talks with govt.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Friday talks were under way with the government on foreign exchange controls, but gave no signals on steps favoured by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel.

Stals, who briefed negotiators at the statutory National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac) forum on monetary policy, told Reuters afterwards in reply to a question on whether talks had begun: "Yes, very much so."
The central bank governor said the cabinet and Manuel had a wide range of options open to them, adding: "What exactly the minister and cabinet will decide one should not speculate on."

Stals said earlier this month he would advise the government that controls be relaxed to permit private individuals to take money out of the country, and for special bonds to be created to allow emigrants to access blocked funds over a number of years.
Many financial analysts now expect Manuel to make an announcement on the further easing of forex controls in or around his March 12 budget.
Stals said market expectations could push Manuel into addressing the issue at budget time:
"There's so much speculation and expectations, so obviously the minister will have to say something -- even if he says he's going to do nothing, he'll have to say it."
